transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

The flashing 'U' code on Beko induction hobs typically means the hob cannot detect a suitable pan. This is rarely a fault with a brand-new unit; it usually happens if the cookware isn't magnetic (like aluminium or copper) or isn't flat enough. Please check that your saucepan has a magnetic base and place it squarely in the centre of the zone, then press the 'Start' button. If you have another pan that works on an induction hob elsewhere, try that one to confirm.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
Hmm, a fridge magnet doesn't stick to my saucepans, but it does stick to my cast-iron casserole, and that one heated fine. The pans are aluminium and old. So is the hob actually okay?

Yes, the hob is perfectly okay. The 'U' code simply means it cannot detect a magnetic pan because your aluminium saucepans are not induction-compatible. Since the cast-iron casserole worked fine, we have confirmed the appliance and installation are correct. You will need to use specific induction-compatible cookware (where a magnet sticks firmly) for this hob to work.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

candidates: Incorrect zone selection or pan placement (medium)
Hob control board fault (less likely on new unit) (low)
